01

The mark

The wordmark is the client’s own and is not redrawn here. What this build adds is how it behaves: it sits in a perspective container in the header and turns on a slow idle loop, paused on hover. Two findings came out of auditing the files, and both are noted below.

Open · no standalone markThere is no monogram. A wordmark 668px wide by 276px is being scaled into a 32px browser tab, where it can only ever be a smear. IAQ needs one glyph, most likely the Q, drawn for small sizes.
Open · unused fileThe dimensional render is not referenced by any page. Either it belongs somewhere deliberate, or it should come out of the assets folder.
Header height46px, in a 600px perspective, on a ten second idle turn. Reduced motion holds it at a fixed angle.
Clear spaceThe height of the Q on all four sides. Nothing crosses it, including the nav’s own links.
Minimum size96px wide. Below that the wordmark stops being legible and there is currently nothing to fall back to.
NeverDo not recolour it, put it in a container, or place it over a busy part of a photograph.
02

Brand elements

What every IAQ piece is built from, and when to use each part. It all comes out of the wordmark: IAQ is drawn in seven horizontal lines, so IAQ’s graphics are horizontal lines, squares and slim boxes, in red, white, black and navy. Measurements are read from IAQ’s own vector logo (2024.02.29) and measurement file; the file is named beside each one. Section 19 uses nothing that is not defined here, and section 03 holds the references it follows.

The lockup

IAQ’s own artwork, never rebuilt: the wordmark with “Your Total Facility Solutions Provider” set beneath it (IAQ, logo with tagline, 2024). The line is part of the artwork, so it is never retyped in another face.

Colour

Four colours, and IAQ is known for using both black and navy. The red and the black come from the logo file itself. Nothing yellow, ever: no amber, no gold, no warm filter.

Fonts

Rigid, strong and robust, never thick. Two faces, the same two as the website: Switzer carries every name, headline, figure and label; Instrument Sans carries sentences. Both are free for commercial use (Switzer from Fontshare, Instrument Sans from Google Fonts). Word and Outlook documents fall back to Arial, which is also the face of the line in IAQ’s lockup artwork.

The line

The line IAQ always uses: one long, thin, red line, left to right, across the whole piece or the whole column. It may be separated the way the wordmark’s own rows are: the top row is one line in three (I, A, Q), the bottom row one line in four (I, the two feet of the A, Q). It is refined: a quarter of one wordmark bar thick at the logo size on that piece. It is never short.

The seven lines

IAQ’s identity, and a texture rather than a headline: ten to fifteen percent of a piece. The seven lines are the wordmark’s bars at their exact thicknesses and gaps, run long, left to right, full bleed. Five lines, the middle five bars, where seven would be too tall. Always at the foot or the head of a piece, never behind type.

The delivery cycle

The way IAQ presents its workflow, its design and its brand: six stages on one fine ring, the active stretch of the ring in red, each stage a white disc holding a grey isometric object, and one clean isometric visual at the centre that changes with the stage. Use it whenever IAQ explains how it works.

How it is drawn

  • The ring: one fine line, the one curved line IAQ draws; the stretch between the active stage and the next is red.
  • The discs: white, the same size, a soft lift and nothing else; the active disc takes a red ring.
  • The objects: grey isometric renders, one per stage, from the object set in section 06.
  • The centre: one isometric visual of the stage, white and grey with its red part, on white, looping quietly.
  • The labels: number and name in capitals beside each disc; the active one in red.
  • Motion: it steps to the next stage every three seconds until the reader touches it.
  • Never a second colour on the ring, a filled disc, or type on the centre visual.

Slim boxes and containers

IAQ contains things in slim horizontal boxes: black, red or navy with white type, or white with red type on a red ground. They are the buttons, the labels, the values in a table and the plates on a wall. Square corners, one line of type, at least four times as wide as they are tall.

The square and the texture

IAQ’s world is square. Markers are squares, textures are squares, figures can be built from squares. Round dots belong to other brands.

The construction wireframe

IAQ designs and engineers what it builds, so its pieces may show their construction: fine lines behind the layout, the rows of the wordmark, diagonals, a dimension. Horizontal and diagonal only, red at a third on white or white at a fifth on red and navy, never behind a sentence.

Visuals: when, and when not

A visual earns its place when it shows the real thing IAQ built, installed or runs. Otherwise the piece is type, lines and colour, which is what most of IAQ’s pieces are.

Use a visual

  • One per piece. A facility IAQ delivered, a cleanroom, plant, people at work.
  • As a clean block. Square corners, aligned to the margins, no fade, no frame.
  • In true colour, the yellow cast taken out and nothing else: tools/design-grade-0925.py.
  • Where no photograph exists, an isometric object or a drawn scene from section 06.

Leave it out

  • Never type on a visual. Type sits beside it, above it or below it.
  • Business cards, letterheads, signatures in replies, signage and plates: no photograph.
  • A figure or a statement is the visual: 250+, ISO Class 1.
  • Stock and generated pictures of work IAQ did not do.

Gradients

IAQ separates with strong blocks, squares and long lines, not with gradients. Colour meets colour at a clean edge.

Where a gradient may appear

  • Inside a photograph or a render: its own light, never added.
  • On screen, behind 3D and the dotted globe: the dark stage’s own falloff, where nothing is written.

Everywhere else, none

  • No fade from a photograph into a colour.
  • No gradient on a ground, a box, a button, a line, an icon or type.
  • No glow, no shadow on flat artwork.

Badges

The certification bodies’ own artwork, untouched and in full colour, always on white. On red or navy they sit in a white container. One height for all, in one row, at the foot of the piece, with the standards named once beside them.

The element library

Everything above, as a kit to design with. Each card says when to use the element, how, and what never to do with it.

Boundaries

The edges of the system, for design and for language. Anything outside them is not IAQ, however good it looks.

Design

  • No vertical line, of any weight, anywhere.
  • No short dash and no small block of stripes. Lines run the width.
  • No gradient, fade, glow or drop shadow on artwork.
  • No type on a photograph, and one photograph per piece at most.
  • No rounded corner, round dot or pill. Circles only where the thing is round.
  • No yellow, and no colour outside red, white, black and navy on a printed piece.
  • No blue, black or grey line.
  • No change to the wordmark: no recolour, no outline, no retyped line, never on a photograph.
  • No heavy type, 700 and above, and no rounded or soft faces.

Language

  • No dash as a pause or a separator. The middle dot joins facts; “to” writes a range.
  • No exclamation mark.
  • No negative statement in client facing copy: say what IAQ does.
  • No superlative and no claim without a source: figures first, published figures only.
  • No capitals for a sentence; capitals live only in slim boxes.
  • No ampersand in running sentences, only inside proper names.
  • No client name without IAQ’s permission, and no invented person or number.
  • Always sentence case, one idea per sentence, the reader’s benefit stated plainly.
03

Art direction

The seventeen references Bazil set for IAQ’s mockups and art direction, kept here as the standard every IAQ piece is measured against. Each says what IAQ takes from it, and what IAQ changes, because every one of them carries at least one thing IAQ never does. Internal reference only: these are other studios’ work, and this folder never ships with the site.

04

Colour

One accent, and it is the client’s red. Everything else is a near-neutral: a cool paper, white panels, and three weights of ink. The site has no second brand colour, which is what lets the red mean something every time it appears.

The rule that keeps it clean: a section is either paper or dark band. There is no third surface, and no colour is introduced to separate two things that a hairline can separate.

The kind colours (Bazil, 25 Sep 2026)

Five kinds of thing recur across the site, and each carries one colour wherever it appears: in a title, a chip, a tag, a connector, a mark. The red stays the brand accent; the others belong to their kind only.

The rules that came with the colours. Kind titles are numerals in the kind's colour, one size, the kind's flat mark at the left: "6 services", "3 business units", "4 works". Icons are flat line marks in the kind's colour, never in a box; on the markets they are violet with white accents, never red. The market pages are violet throughout: the headline phrase, the marks, the labels and the numbers, with the red kept for buttons. Isometric marks (the six service objects) are fitted to one box, drawn without shadows, ground ellipses or CSS scaling, so their edges stay crisp. Connectors on the facility map are thin ribbons, 3 px, running from the colour of the card they leave to the colour of the card they reach. Tables of kinds keep their labels in the cells (the unit's name, "when you ask"); symbols alone were tried and rejected.

Their palette, and ours

IAQ’s Revit coordination model is colour-coded by system, and the fifty-seven frames they exported from it are in the repository. Those colours are theirs and they are correct: fire protection is red because sprinkler pipework is red on site.

Structural Architectural Process utilities Fire protection Air-conditioning Electrical Cleanroom Tools hookup

The site does not render them. Nine saturated hues at one value read as a toy rather than a facility, and they fight the one colour this brand owns. The scroll assembly separates the systems by value instead, a ladder of true greys from the concrete at the bottom to the cleanroom at the top, with fire protection as the only colour.

Structural Architectural Process utilities Fire protection Air-conditioning Electrical Cleanroom Tools hookup

Open decision. Accurate to their drawing and on-brand pull in opposite directions here. This is the on-brand answer; the faithful one is one edit away.

05

Type

Three families, one job each, and one ladder underneath them. Every size, line-height, tracking and measure below is read out of src/styles/base.css and the page stylesheets. Where a value is a clamp() the clamp is printed instead of a single number, because the build is fluid and on a fluid page the clamp is the value. The specimens are set with the same declarations, so this is the scale itself rather than a picture of one.

01 · Switzer · 400 500 600 700 Engineering controlled environments

Every heading, every display numeral, every short caps label, every button. One face carries the whole voice of the interface.

h1,h2,h3{font-family:"Switzer",sans-serif;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.02em;line-height:1.06;text-wrap:pretty}
02 · Instrument Sans · 400 500 600 Designed, built and maintained by one team.

Running sentences only: ledes, body copy, card descriptions, table cells. Never a heading, never a label.

body{font-family:"Instrument Sans",system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6}
03 · JetBrains Mono · 400 500 700 03 · 1,240,000

Digits that have to line up in a column, and nothing else. Nine declarations in the whole build call it.

--num:"JetBrains Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;

What changed on 9 September, and why. Every small uppercase label on this site used to be JetBrains Mono. At 9.5px with .16em of tracking a typewriter face reads as a terminal, not as a label on an industrial site, and the client asked for it out. --label now resolves to "Switzer","Instrument Sans",system-ui,sans-serif, so the 324 places the stylesheets call it share the headline voice one size down. --num kept the monospace, because tabular alignment is a real job and only digits need it.

Numerals

Sixteen declarations across eleven stylesheets set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, and between them they cover every figure a reader can compare: counters, years, market indices, ledger counts, banner fact figures. A proportional 1 beside a proportional 8 makes a column of numbers ripple, and a count that animates upward shifts its own width on every frame. A number that can be compared to another number is tabular. A number in the middle of a sentence is not.

The family is a separate decision from the figures. Display numerals stay in Switzer, because a figure at 126px is a heading. Mono is reserved for a figure that indexes something: all nine --num declarations are a stage number, a year, a count or a row reference.

The small-screen floor

Set on 4 September, after the client asked for a more professional mobile view. Prose was shrinking to between 11px and 12.5px on phones across every page, which is the loudest cheap signal a small screen can give. A real sentence now holds 13px and supporting copy 13.5px, and nothing under 640px is allowed below that. The lower bound of every clamp above already clears the floor, so the floor only has to catch the rules that override a clamp on a phone. Two of them get larger on a phone, which is the point.

RuleDesktop640px and under
.head h1clamp(32px, 4.8vw, 58px)clamp(28px, 8vw, 38px)
.pg-head h1clamp(30px, 4.6vw, 56px)clamp(26px, 7.6vw, 36px)
.pg-sec h2clamp(23px, 3.1vw, 36px)clamp(20px, 6vw, 27px)
.pg-head-ledeclamp(15px, 1.7vw, 18px)14px
.pg-ledeclamp(14.5px, 1.6vw, 17px)13.5px / 1.55
.ledeclamp(16px, 1.8vw, 18.5px)15px / 1.55
.pg-pc h3 project card title16px13.5px
.mk-cb p market card sentence12.5px13px / 1.45
.pg-pc .pg-cl client line12.5px13px
.pg-tag10px / .08em7.5px / .06em

The tag is the exception, and it is deliberate. A tag drops to 7.5px on a phone where a sentence may not go under 13px, because a tracked single word is scanned, not read. The 4 September note that set the floor calls those labels “mono”: that was true when it was written and stopped being true five days later, when the label family moved to Switzer. The floor itself did not change.

Where mono is wrong. A monospaced face squares every glyph to one width, so a run of real words in it becomes a block of rectangles. On 9 September the scope list in the 3D rail was moved off it: the list had been JetBrains Mono, uppercase, tracked out at 10px, and it wrapped to three lines. It now runs Switzer at 12.5px, weight 500, tracking 0, in sentence case. The count beside it kept the mono, because on a count the alignment is the whole point.

06

Icons

One drawn mark per discipline, each one showing the system as a drawing set would show it, in section or elevation. They are drawn to the house spec, shared with the interface set: a 24 unit grid, one stroke weight of 1, butt caps and mitred joins, no fill. Straight lines and full circles only, which is the whole vocabulary of that set. They inherit currentColor, so a stage’s own colour carries its mark and the same nine files serve the dark stage.

The icon library, as the site draws it today

Every icon set from the live components, in the kind colours: services red, units in three blues, work amber, systems green, markets violet with white on navy, delivery models and interface marks ink. Never in a box. The live, animated version is on the portal’s Design direction page; this copy is regenerated by tools/export-icons.mjs.

What these replaced, and why. The first set was stock pictograms: a neoclassical bank for civil and structural, a pitched house for architectural on a semiconductor fab, a lightning bolt for electrical containment, a briefcase for tools hookup. None of them is a thing IAQ builds. They were also drawn with square caps and mitred joins, which is what made every corner read blocky. A second pass was needed after that, because four marks that looked acceptable at 19px in the rail were misreading at 96px: a circus tent, a tap with a spout, a broom and a barn. Judge an icon at size, then judge it again at four times the size.

And two more passes, the same day. A version with two pen weights was tried and rejected: on a mark this small a second weight does not read as hierarchy, it reads as a mistake. So did the arcs. Every pipe elbow, cable sag and spray curve is gone, because a straight run drawn bent is wrong however well it is drawn. Final spec: one weight of 1 on a 24 grid, butt caps, mitred joins. A mitred corner is the more correct answer on a drafted mark anyway. A pile cap has a corner, not a fillet.

On the dark band

Every mark is stroke-only and inherits its colour, so the same nine files serve the dark stage without a second set. This is the set as the 3D rail shows it, at 22px and a 1.15 stroke: at 19px and 1 the line came out under a device pixel on a near-black ground and the marks simply were not there. The rail and the model both keep the nine system colours, because a coordination model that renders every system the same value has stopped coordinating.

The same nine, isometric

A second cut of the set for places a line mark is too quiet: a section opener, a market card, the loading screen. Same subjects, same order, same names, so either set stands in for the other. Solids with three face values rather than line work, built on the same projection helper as the illustration in section 08. Filled faces, no outlines, which is the whole trick: a stroke on a twenty pixel face is noise, and noise is what stops a small isometric object reading. Three fills per box on a tight value ladder, a step darker where one thing meets another, a soft patch underneath so the object sits rather than floats, and one red accent on the part that matters. One element of each moves on a slow loop, because a moving part tells you what a thing does; all of it stops under a reduced-motion preference. Use one set or the other in a given view, never both.

The market set

Superseded 25 Sep 2026. The markets are drawn violet with white accents now, never red; the current set is in the icon library at the top of this section. What follows is the history of how the set was drawn.

23 Sep, and it ended where it should have started. The row was taken all the way to a WebGL scene (src/scenes/market-marks.js, flat toon shading with an inverted-hull outline, still live at ?marks=3d) and then audited part by part: part counts ran 5 to 11 across the seven and the red ran from one small element to a whole textured face, so the set could not read as a set. Under that sits the harder limit, which is scale: a mark is about 90 px on a photograph, and a modelled machine at 90 px has no room for the detail that makes it read as the real thing. The hero carries drawn marks (HeroLineMarks.jsx) on the same house spec as the 41 interface marks and the record block: 24 grid, one weight, butt caps, mitred joins, no fill, one red element each, with a second layer of detail on every subject. The geometry is exported once as LINE_SHAPES and the markets strip draws the same paths, so the hero, the strip and the record block speak once. The 3D is kept for a surface that gives an object 300 px or more.

The four numbers that make it a set. Every mark sits on baseline y = 20, is centred on x = 12, stands 15 to 16 units tall and 13 to 17 wide, and carries exactly one red element that is a real part of the machine. Before this pass the same seven were on the house spec but not on one frame: baselines ran 17 to 22 on a 24 grid, heights ran 12.5 to 19, Bio sat at cx 13.1, the battery's red was three dashes, and the photovoltaic and bottle reds were drawn on top of a grey line that was already there, so they were not elements at all. tools/measure-heromarks.mjs prints the box, the baseline and the red count for all seven; run it after any edit. The row also breathes on one phase now: the float used to carry a −.7s per-tile delay, which on a 5.2s cycle put the seven up to 4.2 px apart at any instant and read as the row being unstructured.

The delivery cycle, as a ring

Same day. Bazil, with a six-node wheel as the reference: the cycle is a ring (CycleRing.jsx) laid out on a fixed 1000 grid so it cannot drift, six nodes at 60 degree steps, the arc from the previous stage into the active one in the client red and trimmed at both ends so it stops at the disc, and the active stage in the centre with its tag, name, line and link. The discs carry the isometric cycle marks (data/cycleMarks.js), not photographs, because that grey isometric object with one red part is exactly what the reference does and what this build already owns. Below 860 px the ring gives way to a numbered list. The serpentine is still there at ?cycle=flow.

The record set

23 Sep, third cut and the one that stands. The isometric graphite version went ("as for this we need it to look less complex"), then the version built from two reference sheets, pale red tints under grey line work, went too ("looks terrible... do your own style premium"). So: monoline and fine, one ink at 1.15 for the subject and 0.85 for what is inside it, on a 48 grid with butt ends and whole-pixel geometry. No fill anywhere, because a wash of tint is decoration and these marks are labels. One red element each, small and exact, always the part that carries the fact and always the part that lifts on the section's slow loop. The mark is set to the number's own size, not above it, so each stat reads as one object. src/components/RecordFlat.jsx.

Kept for reference: the line cut

The cut before it, and a good one on a light page: the same seven subjects in line work only, one weight of red. It died on the dark hero, where line work with no body has nothing to hold it. The seven markets are the equipment IAQ works on, not buildings and not symbols: a process tool, an open rack, a battery pack, a tracker array, a chiller skid, a bioreactor, a filling line. One colour, the client red, and nothing else, drawn as line work on the same 2:1 dimetric as every other mark here, with the detail doing the work: ladders, handrails, jacket ribs, flanges, valves, cable looms, truss legs. One small part of each is solid, and that part is the one that moves. Blocks were tried three times before this and every version read as the same object seven times over: a silhouette has to be earned by the subject, not by the box it sits in. Generated by scripts_marks_flat.mjs.

Kept for reference: the diorama cut, and the two heading marks

The cut before it: filled isometric in the red and a near-black, each on a pale plate with its dot grid and a node on a stalk. It is a good system and it is kept here on purpose, for a light page or a deck where a mark needs its own ground. Generated by scripts_marks_diorama.mjs; two earlier cuts (solid bands in the logo's grammar, and the facilities drawn as buildings) are in src/_backups/home-0922b.

The interface set · 41 marks

This is the larger of the two systems and the one most of the site runs on: the framework diagram, the service and market detail rows, the specification tables and the closing band all draw from it. Same 24 unit grid, same 1 stroke, same butt caps and mitred joins as the nine discipline marks, so the two sets sit together without a seam. Audited 9 September: 41 marks, no exceptions, not one local stroke, fill or override anywhere in the file.

Where this set curves, and why it is not a contradiction. Fifteen of the forty-one use an arc, marked below. Every one of them curves because the thing is curved: a water drop, a leaf, a person’s shoulders, the shoulder of a gas cylinder, a flask, rising steam, air streamlines. Not one bends a straight run. That is the rule the discipline marks were breaking with pipe elbows and cable sag, and it is why they are drawn straight.

The navigation set

Three marks sit in the header. They ran at 16, 17 and 34px glyphs in 38, 38 and 48px boxes, so the cube read as twice the others. One size for the set: a 19px glyph in a 40px box, 44px at the tap-target width, one stroke weight. 19px is the site’s icon size, the same as the marks above.

The icon family, one isometric grammar (25 Sep 2026)

Two to four solids on one grid, three flat tones, one accent in the kind’s colour: red for a service, blue for a unit, yellow for work, green for a system. Drawn by components/IsoIcon.jsx; used on the Services page and the map. Live on the portal’s Design direction page.

Marks: art and motion (Bazil, 25 Sep 2026)

The six value marks from the Culture page. Every new drawn mark on the site starts from these rules. Live and animated on the portal’s Design direction page.

Marks: art and motion, the six services (25 Sep 2026)

Six more drawn scenes on the same rules as the value marks above, so the services have their own set and the site has variety: the dotted drafting ground, ink line work at 1.6, white and one pale grey, the plain number top right, and one movement in IAQ red that says what the service does. Every red movement runs horizontally or turns, never down a vertical line. Each loop runs about six seconds, a beat apart, only while it is on screen; under reduced motion the finished drawing is the still.

Art style

Ground. A dotted drafting ground: one dot every 12 units, #C3CBD8 at 55%. No box, no shadow, no gradient behind the mark.

Line. Ink line work at 1.6, butt caps and mitre joins; fine detail at 0.8, emphasis at 2.2. Fills are white or one pale grey, #E6EAF1.

Colour. Everything is ink except the one element that moves, which is IAQ red. One red thing per scene.

Number. The plain number, top right, light ink at 16%. No prefix, no box.

Scale. Drawn on a 240 by 160 sheet, centred, shown at the card’s full width.

Animation style

One movement. Each scene says its idea in one movement: a count runs the ring, rows tick then the seal lands, the balance swings and settles, a cursor draws then dimensions, the needle overshoots and settles in its band, the podium builds and the trophy fills.

Pace. About six seconds a loop: the movement, a settle with ease-out, then a hold on the finished drawing before it runs again.

Stagger. Cards in a row start a beat apart, so the grid never moves in unison.

When. Only while the card is on screen. Off screen, and under reduced motion, the finished drawing is the still.

10

Photography

Photography on this site means the work: sites IAQ built, plant they installed, people they employ. The one rule the client has repeated more than any other is that words never sit in a box on a photograph. Copy sits on a gradient scrim that darkens toward the edge it reads from, so the image keeps running underneath it.

The colour rule: mostly white, a little red, and no black. A cleanroom is already the right picture, because it is a white room. Choose and grade every photograph toward that: light neutral ground, red only where it genuinely appears on site, and no heavy shadow mass. A warm sunset exterior is off palette however good the shot is.

Open, and worth saying plainly. The market and capability banners on the site are generated, not photographed, and most company photographs in the library are staff and event pictures rather than pictures of the work. One of them carries the logo stamped into the image, which breaks the rule this section opens with. A shoot of two or three live sites, interiors and people at work, would replace all of it and is the single biggest lift available to this site.

Scrim, not a boxLeftA gradient from 86% at the bottom to nothing by two thirds up. The building stays visible behind the words.
The panelRightRejected twice. A filled panel crops the photograph into a strip and makes the page look like a template.
RatiosHeroes run full bleed. Cards and market banners are 16:10. People are 16:10, never square.
VideoMuted, inline, object-fit cover so there are never black sides. A card’s poster frame is static; only the hero loops.
ColourCool daylight or dusk. No warm filters, no heavy grade, and nothing that makes a cleanroom look yellow.
NeverNo stock. If a photograph of the real thing does not exist, the section gets a drawn mark or a diagram instead.
11

Illustration

Where a photograph of the real thing does not exist, the site draws it. There are two art directions, and they are not alternatives: they do different jobs, and a piece of work should be commissioned in one or the other on purpose.

A · DrawnTrue 30 degree isometric in flat vector. Every value is a number in a geometry script, so it recolours, relabels and rebuilds at any size with no illustrator in the loop. It cannot shade, and it should not try: its quality is line, hatching and annotation. Use it for documents, diagrams and anything that has to stay editable.
B · RenderedReal geometry with real lights. Orthographic or near it, a single neutral key, ground truth ambient occlusion, soft shadow maps. It is the only way to get form, contact shadow and depth, and it is what the scroll assembly on the home page runs on. Use it for showpieces.
B · Rendered · this is the site’s own scroll assembly, running live · scenes/fab3d.js · drag to turn, scroll inside it to build
The subject is theirsNot a generic factory. This is the assembly the site already tells: foundation and sub-fab services, the fab floor and its process tools, the cleanroom ceiling and its fan filter units, the roof with ductwork, plant and the exhaust stack.
Exploded, not cut awayA cutaway hides eight of the nine systems behind a slab. Four trays lifted on one axis, with the assembly guides running through them, shows all of it and says built in order at the same time.
One accentRed marks what is genuinely red on site: the fire main, the gas cabinet, the stack cap, one fan filter unit under test. It is never used to decorate a shape.
Neutral greysEvery grey is a true grey with no blue and no warmth. That is the only reason the red reads as loudly as it does.
Three facesTop white, left #EDEDED, right #D2D2D2, outlined in #101010. Interiors and recesses are near-black, which is what gives a white object its depth.
Detail carries the weightLouvred plant, ruled coils, flanged duct joints, a cat ladder up the stack, dark process chambers, handrails round the roof deck. A solid box reads as a block; what is on a surface is what makes it read as equipment.
Held back on purposeThe envelope that is not built yet is a dashed ghost. The ties between trays are hairlines with a single red node. The crane is a shade of grey lighter than the plant it is landing. Detail everywhere and emphasis nowhere is just noise.
Steel is a latticeThe crane mast and jib are drawn as chords and web, not as bars. It is the difference between a drawing that says structure and one that says rectangle.
Coded, not drawnA projection helper gives boxes, cylinders, discs, runs, ruled faces, hatching, lattice, handrails and cast shadows. The scene is composed back to front by hand, because an exploded assembly is not a depth sort.
B · Rendered, the paletteThe scroll assembly carries the nine BIM system colours from IAQ’s own coordination model, one hue per system, so the rail and the model always agree about what you are looking at. It was flattened to a grey ladder for half a day and put back: nine systems that all read as the same white building is a coordination model that has stopped coordinating. Fire protection is a true red because it is red on site.
B · Rendered, the lightA warm key and a cool fill, which is what a coloured model wants: the cast separates the lit face from the shaded one without washing the hues out. Ambient occlusion carries the contact shadow under every beam, pile cap and tool foot, and the shadow map is 2048 so a soft edge does not stair-step.
The geometry that mattersHow much room a lifted tray has is not the gap. A point is behind the slab above exactly when x + dz ≤ W and y + dz ≤ D for dz = zup − z, so the visible height at a spot is GAP − TRAY − (D − y₂): it depends on how far FORWARD the object stands. At 6.4 the back metre of every tray showed nothing at all and the back column line lived in it. The gap is 8.4.

12

Grid and space

The whole site is one container token and one gutter token, and every full width band carries the gutter inside its own padding rather than borrowing a wrapper. From 1025px up the root element carries a CSS zoom, which means viewport units on this site do not measure the viewport. Anything doing maths against the screen has to read that part first.

Container--maxw: min(100%, 1900px)

The shell runs edge to edge on the client’s instruction of 25 August, take the whole space left and right. The min() only bites on an ultrawide monitor, so a line of prose never stretches past reading length.

Gutter--gut: clamp(14px, 1.5vw, 26px)

The smallest gutter that still keeps type off the bezel. It is a token, never a literal: every band on every page resolves its left and right padding from this one declaration.

Gutter above 1600px--gut: clamp(24px, 4.4vw - 46px, 64px)

Replaced the flat 26px cap on 4 September. Nothing was misaligned: 26px is 1.3% of a 2000px screen, so on a large monitor the whole site read as printed to the edge of the paper. The formula is continuous at the breakpoint, 24px from the old rule against 24.4px from the new one, so dragging a window across 1600px shows no step, and it reaches the 64px cap at 2500px. Declared twice, on :root and on body.page-home, because the home page redeclares the token at its own specificity and would otherwise ignore the base rule.

Gutter at 640px and under:root { --gut: 14px }body.page-home { --gut: 16px }

Locked to a pixel rather than left fluid. Below this width the clamp floor is already in force, so a formula would only be a slower way of writing 14.

Who owns what.pg-sec { padding: X var(--gut) Y }.pg-in { max-width: var(--maxw) }

The band owns the horizontal gutter, the inner element owns the width. Written into the shared page stylesheet as a standing rule after a two class selector outranked .head.wrap and flattened a page against the screen edge. No band in the phase two system depends on .wrap.

Every trackminmax(0, …)

No grid track in the shared page system is allowed an implicit auto minimum. An auto minimum is what lets one long word push a whole page sideways.

Two section systems.sec.pg-sec

The home page runs .sec from its own stylesheet. The other eighteen pages import the shared phase two stylesheet and run .pg-sec. Both read the same tokens, and the numbers differ, which is why they are listed separately in the rhythm table below.

Gutters drawn at their 26px cap. Above 1600px each one opens toward 64px, below 640px both hold at 14px.

.pg-splitThe standard two column band: argument left, support right.

The 300px floor is why the rail never crushes into an unreadable strip before the 900px breakpoint stacks it. Gap clamp(24px, 4vw, 64px).

.f-nav-wideThe footer sitemap: brand on the left, the link columns pinned right.

The build carries 22 distinct max-width values across 183 max-width media queries, and five of them, 640, 900, 760, 820 and 960, account for 134 of those. The rest are component local: one grid, one rail, one caption. That is the honest reading of the stylesheets, not a scale designed in advance. A component breakpoint that only moves its own tracks is safe. Anything that moves the shell belongs on one of the five.

Below 1025px1.00No zoom. --zoomf is undeclared, so every consumer falls back to 1.
1025px and up1.12Type was small on a real desktop monitor. Zoom reflows the responsive layout instead of scaling a fixed canvas, so nothing overflows.
2240px and up1.50The 2K tier, added 28 August alongside the 4K one.
3200px and up2.10The 4K tier. Each tier holds the effective layout width near the 1700 to 1900px the design was proofed at, so a 4K screen sees that composition scaled rather than a 1900px strip floating in a void.

The trap the zoom carries

Viewport units on this site do not measure the viewport. The zoom sits on the root element, and viewport units resolve against the unzoomed window before the zoom scales the result. A stage declared 100vh paints 1008px tall in a 900px window and pushes the page down by the difference. Anything sized in vh, vw, svh or dvh that has to match the real screen divides by --zoomf.

.fab-stage { height: calc(100svh / var(--zoomf, 1)); } .hero { min-height: min(calc((86svh - var(--tbh, 0px)) / var(--zoomf, 1.12)), 786px); }

The fallbacks differ on purpose. .fab-stage is declared outside any media query, so below 1025px the fallback of 1 is the value that applies. The hero rule lives inside the 1025px query, so its 1.12 fallback never fires and only names the tier it sits in. The 786px cap is one number written twice: 786 multiplied by 1.12 is the 880 painted pixels the hero is allowed, set after the client said the banner was too tall for a website.

The same trap has two more faces. Script has to read the zoom, never assume it. There are three tiers, so the /home2 route reads getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).zoom and republishes the true viewport as --vpw and --vph before its scroll triggers measure anything. And a bounding rect is not a CSS pixel. getBoundingClientRect() returns painted pixels, while a value written back into top or paddingTop is read inside the zoom and scaled a second time. Measuring the workspace bar with the rect left an 8px strip of page showing between the bar and the nav, which is why that bar is measured with offsetHeight.

BandPaddingFluid between (window height)At 640px and under

.pg-headclamp(40px, 6.5vh, 78px) var(--gut) clamp(20px, 3.2vh, 34px)615 to 1200px, top edge28px var(--gut) 22px
.secclamp(44px, 7vh, 82px) 0629 to 1171px26px 0
.pg-secclamp(38px, 6vh, 74px) var(--gut)633 to 1233px30px var(--gut)

The rhythm is measured against the height of the window, not its width. A short laptop screen gets tighter bands than a tall monitor, which is the axis the reader is actually short of. Every one of these carries the zoom with it: from 1025px up the vh is computed against the unzoomed window and then painted 12% larger, so the 82px cap on .sec reaches the eye as 92px. The cap is what is in the stylesheet, the number on screen is that cap times --zoomf.

A step scale is declared and never used. --s1 through --s8, at 8, 14, 20, 28, 38, 52, 70 and 96px, sit on the home page body, six of the eight are redeclared smaller at 640px, and no rule in the build reads any of them. The rhythm is carried by clamp() on the band instead, because a fixed step cannot answer the viewport and section padding is the one measurement that has to. Read the clamps above, not the scale.

13

Motion

Motion on this site is one curve, five rungs of duration, and a hard stop for anyone who has asked for less of it. It was three rows of the layout table, easing, hover and reduced motion, which is not enough room for a curve that appears 254 times in the stylesheets. Every curve below is plotted from its own control points and run at one slowed length, so what you compare is shape. The ladder under it runs at real speed.

The curvesFive carry the site. One of them does almost all the work.
--e1 cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) 254 uses · 28 stylesheets

The default. Fast off the mark, long settle, no overshoot. Declared in base.css:20 and again at body.page-home scope in home.css:14, because home.css loads after base.css and a page token has to win on source order. One curve for everything that moves: a second curve reads as a second designer.

--e2 cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) 7 uses · 4 stylesheets

The sharper start. Same family, quicker off zero, for a small object that has to feel instant under the pointer: the 4px square marking the hovered tab, base.css:119, and the mega panel opening at base.css:132. It is a token only inside body.page-home, so six of its seven uses are written out longhand. That is why it has 7 uses and --e1 has 254.

no token cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.25,1) 23 uses · one file

The milestone marks. A shallower launch than --e1, so an object dropping onto its ground line reads as weight rather than as a slide. It stays untokenised because it belongs to one file: the choreography was moved out of the page stylesheets when two homepage concepts started showing the same six objects, and a choreography copied into two files is one that drifts.

no token cubic-bezier(.55,.06,.68,.19) 2 uses · home.css:468, 469

The only ease in on the site. On the 3D ring the outgoing stage visual leaves fast and hard on this curve, and the incoming one arrives on --e1 after a 140ms delay. Both used to cross fade on the same curve, which left the centre double occupied and the change read muddy. The 140ms is the number that matters: it clears the frame before the next stage lands in it.

no token cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) 1 use · base.css:167

The one overshoot, and the plot leaves the frame to prove it. It carries the burger lid 4.6px over .55s, because a lid is a physical object being opened. It is the only overshoot in the site chrome.

The duration ladderRead from the 359 transitions in the shipping stylesheets. Bars fill at real speed on a linear ramp, so what you judge is length and not shape.
250ms

Colour only. .wsw a at base.css:66 runs background .25s,color .25s. Of the 87 colour transitions on the site, 27 sit at .25s and 19 at .2s. A colour has no distance to cross, so anything longer reads as lag rather than as a response.

300ms

A displacement of 4px or less. The arrow on a card travels translateX(4px) on transform .3s var(--e1), pages.css:120. Same rung for the footer link rule that draws itself to width, base.css:241.

450ms

The object itself. A card lifts translateY(-4px) on transform .45s var(--e1) and its border turns red on .35s in the same declaration, so the edge has settled before the card has. border-color .35s,transform .45s var(--e1) is the most repeated card declaration on the site: 12 times across 7 stylesheets. Panels sit just under it, at .4s for the mobile drawer.

900ms

An image, inside a frame that does not move. .pg-cardv img goes scale(1.02) to scale(1.06) over transform .9s var(--e1), pages.css:108. The frame is already clipped, so nothing reflows. The nav panel lead image runs the same idea at 1.1s, base.css:533.

1.6s

The hero video arriving. .hero-video video fades on opacity 1.6s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), home.css:101. Long enough that the still frame underneath is never caught being swapped out.

Loops sit outside the ladder because they never resolve: the fab rail icon breathes on 2.6s and the proof marquee runs 36s linear infinite. One more rung is 0s, which appears five times, four of them on visibility. At base.css:132 the mega panel carries visibility 0s .34s, so it stops taking clicks the instant it has finished leaving rather than while it is still fading.

Motion carries meaningFive treatments in src/lib/motion.js, chosen by what the element is rather than by where it sits on the page.

The audit scored motion 3 out of 10 on one line: four animation libraries produce generic fades. One opacity:0, y:24 on everything is a default, not a system, and only two pages had even that. Services, markets, capability, news and the shortlist arrived completely still. One module replaced all of it. The difference between premium and templated is that these five are not the same animation at five delays.

headHeadings 0.95s power4.outy 22 · opacity .001 · blur 7px · top 88%

Type coming into focus, not type sliding in. Opacity starts at .001 rather than 0, so a stalled frame can never leave a headline blank. The blur is dropped with clearProps once it lands, because a permanent filter:blur(0) is a composite cost for nothing.

kickEyebrows 0.6s power3.outx -14 · top 92%

Leads the heading in by a beat and travels sideways, so the two are not one gesture at two speeds.

bodyLede and body copy 0.8s power3.outy 12 · delay .06 · top 90%

Small, slow, unshowy. This is the text someone is trying to read, so it does not perform.

gridCard and stat grids 0.7s power3.outy 18 · scale .985 · stagger .075 · top 86%

The stagger is the whole point: it says these are several of a kind, counted, rather than one block that faded. The marks use the same idea in CSS, stamping --mk-d at .085s per child so six objects arrive in reading order.

figFigures 1.15s power2.outscale 1.08 · top 92%

A release from a held scale inside a frame that is already clipped, so it needs no wrapper and cannot reflow anything.

These five are named, not plotted. They run on GSAP power eases, which are not CSS cubic beziers, so drawing them beside the five curves above would be a drawing of something else. The reliability rules matter more than the values. Every treatment is a gsap.from with immediateRender:false, so the hidden start state is never painted until the trigger actually fires: delete the module and the page is still readable. once:true everywhere, so motion is earned once and the page then rests. Every trigger carries the id iaq-mo and is killed by that id on route change, because a blanket kill would take the pinned showpieces down with it. A sweep releases anything armed, on screen and still invisible, since a trigger measured against a layout that later changed can stay armed forever, and this site pins a 3D assembly, which rewrites document height.

Reduced motionWhat actually happens when the operating system reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Read from the files, not from intent.
Coverage25 of 35 · 7 of 13

25 of the 35 shipping stylesheets carry a prefers-reduced-motion block. 7 of the 13 scene and library modules read the query in JavaScript.

Scroll revealssrc/lib/motion.js

The module returns before a single tween is built. Nothing has to be undone, because nothing was ever created, and the elements simply stay in the state the stylesheet gave them.

Nothing is hiddenhome.css:873

[data-reveal] appears in exactly one CSS rule on the whole site, and that rule is the reduced motion one: opacity:1!important;transform:none!important. The hidden state only ever exists in JavaScript, so a stylesheet alone can never strand a paragraph invisible.

The global damphome.css:871 · careers.css:117

*{animation-duration:.001ms!important;transition-duration:.05ms!important}. Near zero rather than zero: a transition that lasts no time at all fires no transitionend, and anything waiting on one would wait for good.

Hover holds stillpages.css:336 to 339

The transition comes off every card, rail item and next link, and the hover transform is cancelled outright. A card under the pointer does not lift, and the image inside it does not push past its frame.

The pinned assemblyfab-assembly.css:161

The scroll runway is given back: .fab goes height:auto, the stage returns to position:relative, every stage detail opens to max-height:none and opacity:1, and the scroll cue is hidden. The section becomes a document instead of a scrubbed animation, with none of its content withheld.

The marksmark-motion.css:35

The entry choreography, keyframes included, is declared inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Under reduce there is nothing to switch off, because nothing was ever declared. This is the strongest form of the contract and the one the demos in this section copy.

The 3D scenefab3d.js:1641, 1769

The camera is set to its home yaw and pitch and one frame is rendered. On entering view the scene calls render() once instead of starting the animation loop, so the model is fully there and the GPU is idle. The file states the rule in one line: reduced motion gets the destination, not the journey.

The specimens above obey their own section. Every animation in it is declared inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). With the preference set, each square rests at the end of its track and every bar is already full: the destination, not the journey.

Drawn scenesThe six value cards on Careers. A static glyph cannot carry an abstract value, so each value is a small technical drawing whose ONE movement, in IAQ red, says what the value means. Live below, on the same code the site runs.
The frameA 240 by 160 drafting ground with a dotted grid, preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet", so the scene scales with its card and never crops.
The lineInk at 1.6, butt caps, mitre joins, no fill on the line work. Plates are #E6EAF1, paper is white. Same grammar as the interface icons and the record marks.
One red, one movementExactly one element is IAQ red and it is the thing that moves: the count, the ticks and seal, the level, the cursor and dimension, the needle and band, the trophy fill. Nothing else animates.
The loop6 to 7 seconds per scene (--vmd), each part on its own keyframes, and a short dip to .18 at the end so the reset reads as a breath, not a jump.
Only on screenIntersectionObserver at threshold: .35 adds .is-live; every animation rule sits under it, so a card off screen costs nothing. Under reduced motion the finished drawing is the still.
Its own clockEach card carries --vmi and the last rule in the sheet, .vm.is-live :is([class]), sets a negative delay from it. It must stay last: an animation: shorthand on any element resets the delay, which is how six cards once blanked together.
Where it livessrc/components/ValueMotion.jsx draws the scenes, src/styles/value-motion.css moves them. This block is generated from both by tools/design-scenes-0924.mjs; re-run it after any edit.
Adding a sceneDraw on the 240 by 160 grid, centre the subject, put the moving part in a <g> with its own class, give it one keyframe set under .vm-NN.is-live, and keep the red to that part.
What it replacedIsometric objects ("very bad on symbolising"), then flat marks in a tinted square ("wants either video or top level animation"). The rule that came out of it: for an abstract value, a drawn scene with one meaningful movement, or real footage, before any icon.
14

Accessibility

Every value below is read out of the shipped stylesheets and components, and every contrast ratio is computed from the hex in base.css. The build has not been through an audit tool or a screen reader, so this section claims no conformance level. It states what the code does, and where the code falls short it says so.

01 Focus

The ring is 2px solid #EC2027 at a 2px offset, on :focus-visible rather than :focus, so a mouse click on a card never draws it and a keyboard tab always does. 22 of the 35 shipped stylesheets carry at least one :focus-visible rule. 40 of the 42 outline declarations across them are that exact value.

Tab through this row to see the live ring
SemiconductorInset ring, offset −2px Company
On a dark band

2px17The default. Icon buttons, chips, filters, footer links.
3px9Anything with a fill or a border of its own, .cta, .cta-ghost, .mk-go, .nr-pill. The ring clears the edge so it is not read as a second border.
−2px8Inside a card or a mega menu row, .nm-lead, .nm-col a, .cap-step. A positive offset would spill onto the neighbour.

Paper #F7F9FC#EC2027Everything on a light ground4.15:1

On a dark ground the ring changes colour, never weight. Brand red on near-black measures 4.47:1, which clears the 3:1 a focus indicator needs. #FF4D55 is the same hue lifted to 6.00:1, and that is the value the dark sections use.

Two exceptions, both real. The values plate draws a 1px ring instead of 2px (.vp-node, .vp-leg in values-plate.css), and the newsroom mark replaces the outline with box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--blue) (.nx-mk). Both are visible. Neither matches the standard.

Where it is thin. The contact form fields set outline: none and mark focus by moving the 1px border from rgba(12,18,32,.15) to #EC2027 (contact.css). Red on white is 4.37:1, so the indicator clears the 3:1 threshold, but it is a colour swap on a hairline that was already there rather than a ring that appears. The field in the demo above reproduces it exactly. Three of the five field patterns on the site do draw the ring at a 1px offset: .nl-pop input, .gate-form input and .lp-form-in input. The investor gate is the second that does not: .ggate-form input sets outline: none and marks focus with a border colour and a lift in the field background.

02 Contrast

Computed from the token hex values in base.css by the WCAG 2 relative luminance formula. Thresholds: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and for non-text such as a focus ring or an icon.

PairWhere it appearsRatioLevel
Aa Ink on paperAll headings and body copy17.73:1AAA
Aa Ink on whiteCopy inside a white row or card18.70:1AAA
Aa Soft on paperSupporting prose, the only grey allowed a sentence7.32:1AAA
Aa Deep red on whiteEyebrows, the emphasised word in a headline, link hover6.85:1AA
Aa White on deep redThe primary button on hover6.85:1AA
Aa White on redThe primary button at rest, 13px uppercase4.37:1Misses AA by 0.13
Aa Red on paperFocus rings, rules, the 2px fill bar under a figure4.15:1Non-text AA
Aa Faint on paperMono labels at 9 to 11px, including form labels3.24:1Fails AA

The one accent buys one failure. White on #EC2027 is 4.37:1, and .cta sets its label at 13px uppercase, which WCAG counts as normal text. The button label at rest is 0.13 short of AA and clears it on hover, because hover goes to #B5121B. Two ways out: darken the resting fill to the deep red, which spends the brand's loudest colour on a hover state, or lift the label to 14px semibold and accept large-text AA at 3:1. Neither has been taken. The red is the client's and it is not being changed here.

Faint is the wider problem. #828B9E at 3.24:1 carries every mono label on a light ground, and contact.css uses it for the form labels above the fields, at 10px. A label a visitor has to read to fill in a field is the worst place on the site for the lowest contrast on the site. Moving those labels to --soft #48536A takes them to 7.32:1 and changes nothing else.

These ratios hold for text on a flat token ground. Copy set over a photograph, in the industry grid and the project hero, is carried by a gradient scrim and is not measured here.

03 Touch targets

The floor is 40px, set in the mobile pass in base.css under the instruction that nothing interactive goes under it. Primary controls are 44px. Drawn here at true size.

SizeWhat holds itRule
44 × 44Search, member login and the burger, below 760px. They are 40 × 40 above it, where a pointer is precise..nav-search, .nav-login, .nav-burger
44 highThe primary button at every width. The comment beside it: 44px is the smallest a primary action can be and still be comfortable to tap..cta { height: 44px }
44 highStage buttons, leadership rows, contact intent buttons, project links..lp-steps button, .cp-person summary, .intent-b, .ps-links a

Two queries, not one. The size floor is width based, @media (max-width: 760px). The padding growth on footer links, chips and sort segments is pointer based, @media (hover: none), (max-width: 820px), so a touch laptop at desktop width gets the larger target as well. Against WCAG 2.2, a 40px floor clears 2.5.8 at AA, which asks 24 × 24. The 44px controls meet 2.5.5 at AAA. The 40px ones do not.

04 Reduced motion

53 prefers-reduced-motion blocks across 25 of the 35 shipped stylesheets, and 45 guards across 30 of the 92 shipped components and scenes. The contract is not that motion stops. It is that the end state is the one that ships.

RuleWhat the code doesRead from
Anything that animates in lands visibleThe reveal state is forced on, not disabled. opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none.values-grid.css .vg-item

The timeline is never constructedgsap.set('[data-reveal]', { opacity: 1, y: 0 }) and an early return before the context opens.ServicesSection.jsx

One gap. html { scroll-behavior: smooth } is set site wide in base.css, and the only reset to auto under reduced motion lives in about.css. On every route except About, an in page jump still animates for a visitor who asked it not to. The fix is one rule in the base file.

Position in a setaria-current="page" / "step" / "true"The five service pages mark their own rail node, FabAssembly marks the live stage, CycleFlow and NewsBanner mark the active node.
Live regionrole="status" aria-live="polite"News result count, Projects and Careers filter readouts, Investors gate error, which the input also points at with aria-describedby.
A live region deliberately silencedaria-live="off"FabAssembly caption. It changes on every scroll tick, so announcing it would be a stream of noise. The stage counter beside it stays polite.
Labelled regionaria-labelledby59 uses, each pointing at the section's own heading id, for example #hxH in HistorySpan and #nxH in NewsroomIndex.
Decoration removed from the treearia-hidden="true"199 uses: the wires, arcs and chips in CycleFlow, the stacked depth layers and the white twin of the logo in Nav, every ornamental SVG.
Text for a reader only.u-visually-hiddenOne utility, in pages.css, used once: PageHead exposes a figure's alt text.

The roles are not the whole pattern. Only CapabilityPage implements the keyboard half of tabs: tabIndex is 0 on the selected step and −1 on the rest, and ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move the selection. Policies and NewsRail expose the same roles without it, so a screen reader announces a tab list whose arrow keys do nothing and whose every tab is its own tab stop.

Missing. There is no skip link in the build, so on every page a keyboard visitor tabs through the whole header before reaching the content: wordmark, tabs, search, member login and the call to action.

What this section is not. No audit tool has been run and no assistive technology has been tested against the build, so no conformance level is claimed. Six things are known to be short and each is written above: white on red at rest, faint on paper, the two field patterns with no ring, two tab lists without their keyboard half, smooth scrolling on every route except About, and the absent skip link. The rest is what the stylesheets and the components contain today.

15

Voice

Two registers write this site and they are kept apart on purpose. IAQ’s own paragraphs are carried verbatim from the company profile and the client copy sheet, marketing adjectives and all. Every connecting sentence is written here, and it states a class, a measure or a number and then stops. A copy-provenance comment at the top of each market page records which is which, element by element, so any line can be traced to the document it came from.

The register, tested against itself. Four lines were replaced during the build. In each case the earlier version described the website, or said nothing the reader could act on. The reason is recorded in the file, next to the line that replaced it.

Registry banner, second sentence

WasOne registry powers filtering, search, related projects and SEO

NowEvery project carries structured tags: industry, location, delivery model and cleanroom class. Filter to the environment you are building and the record narrows to the work that matches it.

The file gives the reason in one line: written to the client buying the site, not to the visitor using it. The replacement names the four tags and tells the visitor what happens when they use them.
Careers header chip

Was8 · Countries, engine-ready

Now450 · People

Two faults in four words. The file records the count as 6 everywhere else on the site, and “engine-ready” is build talk sitting in a label a candidate reads. The replacement is site canon and it speaks to the person looking at it.
Markets hub card spec

WasCooling and power · Energy at scale · Hygienic

Now160 MW · Malaysia’s largest · 40,000 m²

“Cooling and power” restated the first three words of its own description directly above it. The other two said nothing a buyer could act on. All seven cards now carry a measure or a number.
Newsroom closing block

WasThe newsroom, delivered. Mailing list supplied by IAQ.

NowRemoved. The closing block carries the route to IAQ.

A coming-soon notice and internal build talk in the last content block before the footer. It went rather than got restyled: there is no list to write to, so there is nothing to offer.
Punctuation ruleWhat shipsWhy
A dash as a pause · Not used. The separator is the middle dot, and it carries every joined fact on the site: Mon to Fri · 9:00 to 18:00 · GMT +8. A dash asks the reader to guess whether it is a pause, a range or a minus sign.
A dash as a span A–Z Allowed only where the mark stands for a span or a missing value. The registry sort control reads A–Z, and the newsroom month index prints an en dash against a month that has no items.
A range inside a sentence to Written out: ISO 3 to ISO 7, Class 1 to Class 10K, Mon to Fri. It reads aloud, and it cannot be mistaken for the separator.
Exclamation mark 0 None in any line of copy. Exclamation marks in the source are JavaScript negations, CSS !important, or glyphs in a scramble set. The rule is printed above the newsroom editor in the client’s own CMS so it survives IAQ typing their own articles: no client names, no exclamation marks, no hype.
Ampersand & Kept inside the proper names only: the six services, the three business units and the seven markets. Testing & Commissioning, District Cooling & Heating. Written as “and” in every running sentence.
IAQ’s promotional line blockquote + cite Quoted, never asserted. All seven market pull quotes are the company profile’s own sentences with IAQ company profile set beneath them. In our voice they would be marketing. Attributed, they are evidence of what the company says about itself.

Case is decided by the file, not by the screen. Every label on this site is typed in sentence case and turned into capitals by CSS, so a copy correction is never retyped in caps and never lands half in one case and half in the other.

Prose and headings

Nanometer precision, delivered at breakneck speed.

Sentence case, with a full stop. The accent phrase is wrapped in an em and set in the deep red, so emphasis in a heading is a colour and never italics, caps or a second weight.
Labels

Corporate commitment

Corporate commitment

The first line is the string in the page file. The second is that same string rendered, under text-transform: uppercase at 11px with .2em of tracking. Section eyebrows, stage kickers and slot tags are all written this way.
The main caps exception

START A PROJECT

Typed in capitals in the file, because this label decodes on scroll. The scrambler swaps each character for a random glyph from a pool of A to Z without I and O, the digits and a few symbols, so a lowercase letter would settle out of a pool that never held it.
Title Case

Semiconductor Technology Evolves at Breakneck Speed.

Allowed only inside a quotation. This is the profile’s own line on the semiconductor page. Nothing here is written in Title Case in our own voice, and the only place it appears outside a quotation is one of the proper names below.

How a claim is written depends on what stands behind it. There are five states and each has its own sentence shape, so a reader can tell a measured fact from a company statement without being told.

  1. 01
    Verified, and IAQ supplied the figure

    Largest delivered · 43,000 m² · Backend test, probe and assembly plant, Malaysia.

    Published plain, with the unit and the qualifier. No adjective in front of it, because the number is the argument.
  2. 02
    IAQ states it, and no document proves it

    IAQ states it has built the highest standard of cleanroom, ISO Class 1, for a semiconductor project, and delivered it successfully.

    The attribution sits inside the sentence rather than in a footnote, so the reader can weigh it where they meet it. The same page prints the counterweight: classification is proven by test at commissioning, never assumed from the design.
  3. 03
    Verified, but the client is confidential

    Hyperscale data centre in Malaysia. Client confidential, published by scale only.

    The confidentiality rule is printed above the project editor in the CMS: projects publish by location, sector and scope, never by client name. The 160 MW stands on the record by scale alone.
  4. 04
    Not supplied yet

    Business model questionnaire, section B · exact included scope, the level of single-point accountability and risk IAQ carries, and the typical fast-track timeline · supplied by IAQ

    A labelled slot that names the document it is waiting for and who owns it, shipped visible. A gap written down gets filled. A gap covered with invented copy does not.
  5. 05
    In a source, but uncorroborated

    Left out on purpose the RM310 million value, the 56,000 parties served and the 25-year maintenance mandate. Those appear only in the built about-page concept and are not corroborated in any client-supplied document.

    From the provenance comment on the district cooling page. The omission is recorded rather than made silently, so it can be reversed the day a document turns up.

The names are fixed and they are read from data, never retyped. Below is the canonical spelling of each. Anything that draws them reads the same file, which is what keeps the six stages on a service page identical to the six on a market page.

This order is the client’s confirmed priority and it is the order the cards, the routes and the page numbers all use. The site spells it Data Centre, while the profile pull quote on that same page keeps “Data Center Excellence”, because a quotation is not corrected.

Two naming decisions that replaced an earlier one. “Bio LifeScience” is the client’s July rename. The company profile, the live site and the copy sheet all still say “Pharmaceuticals & Hospitals”, while the project registry has already moved to “Bio LifeScience”, so the page and the registry do not yet agree. Open, and worth saying plainly. The em dash survives in four places across three sentences on the live site. 16

Decisions

Eight reversals drawn side by side, and four more listed at the foot. Each one was built, shown, and taken out again. The reason is not summarised here: it is the line the stylesheet already carries, and where a code comment quotes the client, the quote is theirs. Read this before adding anything to the site, because most of what looks like an obvious improvement has already been tried once.

01

Nothing gets a filled panel behind it.

The active stage in the scroll assembly already carried four signals: full opacity against 34%, its mark and number in the system colour, the title in white, and the scope unfolding underneath. The fill was a fifth signal doing the least work and making the most noise. What replaced it is a mark on a line, which is the same grammar as the nav pointer and the eyebrow rule.

“i dont want it to be in a box” Bazil, 10 September · src/styles/fab-assembly.css

02

Sharp corners. border-radius: 0 everywhere.

The note is dated 24 August in two stylesheets: no rounded buttons, no curve, a technical edge. The industry panels draw their edge with outline inset by 1px rather than border, so the line sits inside the panel’s own overflow crop. What is banned is a rounded container, not a round object: the detail diagram calls its step disc the one circle, and the air-conditioning mark is round because a fan is.

Square edges throughout, no rounded buttons, no boxes: the disc is the one circle. Client note, 24 August · detail-diagram.css, industry-grid.css, home2.css

03

Colour that carries meaning in the client’s own drawing is not brand colour.

On 9 September the whole site was neutralised to red, white and black. In the scroll assembly that meant the nine coordination-model hues collapsing to a grey ladder with fire protection as the only colour, the band going dark on light, the ground to paper and the crane to white. It was reverted the same day. Two fixes made during that pass did not come back with it, because they were made for their own reasons: mono stayed out of the numbers, and the excavator stayed out of the scene.

“revert this to the previous design with colours etc” and “revert back previous design colour, it was only for design tab not the whole website” Bazil, 9 September · src/styles/fab-assembly.css, base.css

OpenSection 02 of this tab still presents the grey ladder as the answer, and its values differ from the ones the code actually used. The build reverted on 9 September. One of the two has to move.

04

No eyebrow directly above a heading.

A small uppercase label sitting on top of a title does the title’s job twice: by the time the eye reaches the heading it has already read a quieter version of it. An eyebrow that labels something else, a card, a band or a form, stays, because there it is the only label there is. The rule is a selector, not a markup edit, so the labels are still in the components and can come back with one line.

“try not to have eyebrows on the title and make the title clear” Bazil, 9 September · src/styles/base.css

05

Mono squares every glyph to one width, so it goes on numbers and never on words.

Every small uppercase label on this site used to be JetBrains Mono at 9.5px with .16em of tracking, which reads as a terminal rather than as a label on an industrial site. The scope list in the assembly rail was the worst case: 10px, uppercase, tracked out, wrapping to three lines of rectangles. Switzer was already loaded for the headings, so the labels now share the headline voice one size down. The stage number above it keeps mono, because a column of numerals is where tabular alignment is the point.

“I really need to remove this font type and replace with a better one through the website” and “this weird rectangle font needs to be replaced with a better one” Bazil, 9 September · src/styles/base.css, fab-assembly.css

06

Nothing in a set overlaps another member of the set, and nothing has to be dragged to be read.

The values section is on its fourth attempt and each one failed for a reason the next had to survive: six isometric line drawings said nothing on sight, a radial orbit was called horrible, and a typographic index read well but was only words. The ring of cards that followed failed on all three counts at once. Six cards standing on one cylinder overlap at any rotation, so titles ghosted through each other; there was no visual, only a small mark in a corner; and a card turned to face the camera has no isometric angle left in it.

“look more premium and look good please and add visual for each”, then “maybe more isometric angle like the example i gave” Bazil, 10 September · src/components/ValuesIso.jsx

07

A row of stories is a row, not one story and its offcuts.

The newest story used to lead at double width, which ate half the row and left space for two tiles and a sliver of a third. The section read as one big story with remnants rather than as a newsroom. Six equal tiles fill the row exactly, and the width is computed rather than guessed so it stays exact at any viewport. The right-edge fade went with the lead, because a fade whose job was to cut the seventh tile in half now only dims the sixth.

“can you put 6 content here so it looks better” Bazil, 10 September · src/styles/news-rail.css

NoteThe six-up block sits after the base card rules, not beside flex-basis where it was first written. .nr-card.lead .nr-shot further down the file has the same specificity, so the earlier position lost and the lead kept a 16/9 crop while its five neighbours were 4/3. Source order was the whole fix.

08

A mark carries its own colour. It does not get a container.

Nine bordered tiles stacked down the assembly panel read as a toolbar rather than as nine systems. The active mark is lifted by a glow around the glyph itself, which is the same move as the hairline in decision 01: the signal goes on the thing, not in a box drawn round it. The marks are set at 22px on a 24 grid with a 1.15 stroke, butt caps and mitred joins.

“lets not put icons inside squares” Client, dated 4 September · src/styles/fab-assembly.css

Four smaller reversals, same grammar

The current nav tab WasA red rule under the selected item, competing with the red rule that already means current on the eyebrow, the tabs and the assembly rail. NowThe current page is red and holds it. A 4px square is the pointer, absolutely positioned so nothing on the row shifts, and it works on a touch screen where a hover mark would never appear. Said“do not underline tab when selected, find a better way to represent”Bazil, 9 Sep · base.css
Progress in the assembly rail WasA 2px red spine filling downward on a gradient with a 12px glow. It read as a page loader and was the loudest thing in a panel whose job is to be read. NowA 1px track at rgba(255,255,255,.16). The steps still hang off a spine, and which stage you are on is carried by the stage. Said“i don’t want the red loading bar at the left”Client, 4 Sep · fab-assembly.css
The newsroom arrows WasOne outlined square and one filled black square, sitting in the corner and outweighing the tabs they belong beside. NowThe glyph alone. It darkens on hover and goes red on the way forward. The 40px box is kept as an invisible hit area so the target stays comfortable without being drawn. Said“no boxes at arrow button”Client, 4 Sep · news-rail.css
The arrow on filled buttons WasPinned to every .cta by CSS, so Start a project, Download the pack and Sign in all carried one. NowNo arrow on a filled button, which is already the loudest affordance on the page. Inline text links keep theirs, because there the arrow is the affordance. Said“not need arrow at the button”Client, 4 Sep · base.css

The pattern under all twelve: every rejected version was a second answer to a question the layout had already answered. A fill behind the only bright row. A bar under the only red tab. An arrow on an already filled button. A box around a mark that already carried its colour. Before adding a signal, find what is already carrying it and count.

Provenance

Content IAQ has not supplied is never written for them. It ships as a labelled slot: a dashed frame, a red tag naming exactly what belongs there, and the name of who supplies it. A labelled gap reads as a decision. Stand in text reads as fact, and stand in text is what gets quoted back in a tender. Two changes replaced earlier versions of this component. 3 September, after the client said there were too many lines, the solid outer panel was removed: a solid box wrapping a dashed box is two frames around one idea, and the dashed frame is the one that marks the block as a placeholder. 9 September, the tag followed the site wide label change. It reads var(--label), so when that token moved off JetBrains Mono it went with it: 8.5px mono became 10px Switzer. Mono is now reserved for var(--num), where digits have to line up in a column.

The gate refuses to stand in front of nothing

The capability pack is given in exchange for a work email, which turns an anonymous visit into a named lead. That trade only works if it is honest about itself, so src/components/GatedDownload.jsx holds three rules.

  1. 01
    No file, no form

    If the document has not been supplied, the form does not render at all. The labelled slot renders instead. A gate in front of nothing collects email addresses for a document nobody can send.

  2. 02
    No endpoint, no success panel

    If the enquiry pipeline has no endpoint, the visitor is told and told so plainly instead. The component never shows a success state for a request that went nowhere.

  3. 03
    The file is released either way

    If the submission fails to log, the download still opens. Withholding a public document because our own logging failed punishes the visitor for our problem.

On /services the gate currently renders in its example state: the finished layout with a placeholder document stack and example contents, form fields present but inert, tagged Example content · the file and the final page count are supplied by IAQ. The form note reads “Activates the moment IAQ supplies the document.” Nothing in that state collects an address.
