20

Tokens

Fifteen custom properties sit in the :root block at the top of src/styles/base.css, and three more are declared further down the same file. Every colour, hairline, face, easing curve and width on the site resolves to one of them. This is the whole ledger, values as shipped.

A component reads a token. Never a literal.

That is what lets the site be recoloured from one block, and what lets this tab quote a value instead of describing one. Where the rule is broken, it is written down below rather than tidied away.

Counts are occurrences of var() across the 147 stylesheet and component files under src/, backups excluded.

Colour

8 tokens

The name is history, the value is the truth. --blue and --blue-bright are named for a palette this build no longer has. Both hold IAQ red. Renaming them would touch 372 references and change nothing on screen, so the names stay and this row exists to stop anyone reading them as a colour.

Line

2 tokens
--linergba(12,18,32,.09) · 144 uses
--line2rgba(12,18,32,.15) · 82 uses

Both are --ink itself at low alpha, not a separate grey: rgb(12,18,32) is #0C1220. A hairline therefore takes a tint from whatever it is drawn over instead of laying a flat grey across two different grounds. --line is the default divider. --line2 is for a border that has to hold an edge on its own, with no fill behind the copy to help it.

Type

2 tokens
--label"Switzer", "Instrument Sans", system-ui, sans-serif324 uses across 34 files

Total facility solutions · est. 1994

Set here at 11px with .2em of tracking, the size and tracking .eyebrow uses in base.css. 273 of its uses set 10px or 10.5px on the same line, and it goes up to 22px where a figure has to carry.
--num"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace9 uses across 7 files

04 · 1,240,000 · 2011

1994   2004   2013   2026

15px and 10.5px, the two most common sizes in the build. The mono face never appears above 15px anywhere on the site, and every declaration that uses it also sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums or a fixed count width.

What changed, and why. Until 9 September --label was JetBrains Mono, so every small caps label on the site was a typewriter face doing a job it was never drawn for: at 9.5px with .16em of tracking it read as a terminal, not as a label on an industrial site. Switzer was already loaded for the headings, so the labels now share the headline voice one size down. --num keeps the monospace and only where digits have to line up in a column.

Two of the three faces are not tokens. body names Instrument Sans directly and h1, h2, h3 name Switzer directly, both as literals. Only the label and numeral faces can be swapped from the block. One consequence is already visible: .sv-n asks --num for weight 600, and JetBrains Mono is loaded at 400, 500 and 700 only, so that one specimen renders at 700.

Motion

1 token
--e1cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)256 uses across 29 files

Nearly all of the distance is covered in the first third, then it settles. One curve for everything that moves: the nav slide, the wing menus, the drawer, every card lift.

the token   cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .25, 1), the most common literal, 22 occurrences

Where the one curve rule leaks. 53 literal cubic-bezier() values remain in the stylesheets, 16 of them distinct, across 8 files. The dashed line above is the commonest of them. It is close enough to the token that no one could name which is which on a 300ms transition, which is the argument that it is a duplicate rather than a decision.

Layout

2 tokens in the block, 3 declared elsewhere
TokenValue

What it is for

Uses
--maxwmin(100%, 1900px)

The shell width. Edge to edge, with a cap that only bites on an ultrawide monitor so a line of prose never stretches past reading length.

22
--gutclamp(14px, 1.5vw, 26px)

The side gutter, on the client's instruction for very little padding. Every wrap, nav row and footer row reads it, which is why the whole site moves together. Two overrides follow it, listed under the table.

77
--zoomf1.12 · 1.5 · 2.1

Mirrors the zoom applied at 1025, 2240 and 3200px, so a script or a viewport calculation can read the scale instead of hard coding it. Undefined below 1025px, which is why every reader writes a fallback beside it.

3
--sticktopvar(--navh, 78px), and 0px under html.nav-off

The offset every in page sticky bar pins to. The nav reserves its height while it is on screen and none of it once it has slid away, so a filter bar can sit tight under the nav with no strip of scrolling cards above it.

4
--navhset at runtime, not in CSS

The nav's measured height. Nav.jsx writes it from nav.offsetHeight on mount, so the sticky offset follows the bar when it wraps instead of trusting a constant.

4

The gutter is overridden twice. From 1600px up it becomes clamp(24px, 4.4vw - 46px, 64px). The 26px cap was 1.3% of a 2000px screen, so a large monitor read as printed to the edge of the paper. At exactly 1600px both rules give 24px, so dragging a window across the breakpoint shows no step. At 640px and below it is a flat 14px, the floor stated rather than computed. The 1600px rule also names body.page-home, because the home page redefines the gutter at a higher specificity and :root alone would have been ignored there.

Tokens that have not earned their keep

3
--zoomf3 reads, 2 files

Read once in home.css and twice in fab-assembly.css, always with a fallback written beside it.

--navh4 reads, 2 files

One is --sticktop reading it, two are the home hero pulling itself up under the nav, and one is a milestone's scroll margin in pages.css.

--sticktop4 reads, 4 files

:root always defines it, so the 75px and 78px fallbacks written at those four call sites can never resolve. They are dead numbers that read as live ones.

A property read three or four times is a habit, not a system. They are listed so the next edit either spreads them or deletes them, rather than leaving a third state where a value is half tokenised.

A token is a scope, not only a global. Rebinding one on a subtree re-skins everything inside it with no rule changes: .u-panel-dark in base.css sets --panel: rgba(15,23,40,.82) and every card under it goes dark. No page currently carries the class, and the dark band rebinds exactly these tokens today, which is why a section can invert without a second stylesheet.

Where the block leaks, stated plainly. The accent is also written as a literal in 140 rgba(236,32,39, ...) declarations and 51 hex ones, because a custom property cannot be given an alpha without color-mix(), which appears five times in the build. Recolouring the site today is one edit to --blue plus a search for that rgba triplet. On 9 September a site wide neutralisation was tried and reverted, which is why the site's greys are still blue tinted while this tab's own greys are true grey: the red, white and black discipline was scoped to the Design tab and the 3D scene, not to the site chrome.
